articles.title: Diplomatic Immunity Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Diplomatic Immunity is the eighth main quest of Skyrim, and it's pretty unique. Instead of delving into a dungeon or slaying a dragon, you're
articles.body:
Diplomatic Immunity is the eighth main quest of Skyrim , and it's pretty unique. Instead of delving into a dungeon or slaying a dragon, you're infiltrating a party to try to steal some Thalmor secrets.

Use the links below to jump to key steps in this quest:

Meet Malborn in Solitude and give him your equipment

Create a distraction and get away from the party

Search for information about the dragons returning

This quest begins as soon as Delphine sets off for Riverwood after A Blade In The Dark - you can either go with her or meet her there later. The plan is to hammer out the plan for infiltrating the Thalmor Embassy . You are to meet a trusted contact of Delphine’s named Malborn at Solitude .

Meet Malborn and Give Him Your Equipment

Solitude is in the northwest of Skyrim, not far from Morthal, which you'll have visited during The Horn of Jurgen Windcaller . You can either walk here or pay a carriage to take you to Solitude.

There's quite a lot you can do in and around Solitude, especially if you're making your way here on foot:

On the southern side of Dragon Bridge, the settlement to the southwest of Solitude, you can find two skill books - Mannimarco, King of Worms (alchemy) on an alchemy table and Warrior (block) at the small bandit camp.

The Break of Dawn side quest to unlock the Dawnbreaker sword at the shrine northeast of Dragon Bridge.

The Rear Guard (light armor) on a table in Castle Dour

The Gold Ribbon of Merit (archery) on a table in Fletcher's shop

The Refugees (light armor) in the blacksmith's shop

The Buying Game (speech) in a bookcase in the Bards College

Malborn is slinking about at The Winking Skeever, near the entrance to Solitude. There, Malborn will ask you which possessions you will need smuggled into the Thalmor Embassy (mainly your gear and some lockpicks would suffice).

Find Delphine at the stables outside Solitude and speak to her to receive some suitable party accoutrements. Speak once more to Delphine when you are ready to be whisked away to the Thalmor Embassy.

Upon your arrival, you meet a rather brazen bloke, Razelan. Keep him at the forefront of your mind. After showing your invitation to the Thalmor bouncer and exchanging pleasantries with the Ambassador, Malborn urges you to create a distraction so that you can sneak out.

Grab a Colovian Brandy either from Malborn or the waitress and hand one to Razelan. With his eyes wide, he pledges his loyalty to you, his best and most trusted friend. Ask him to create a distraction and slip out the back with Malborn.

Alternatively, you can talk to Erikur to create a distraction. After listening to his speech, he will begin to harass Brelas. Then, speak to him and offer to talk to her on his behalf. Do so, then return to Erikur and tell him that she said to meet her in her quarters. He'll then create a scene.

Return to Malborn to sneak into the kitchen. He will lead you into a room where you can find your gear. Once you retrieve your gear from the chest, it is up to you to fight off (or sneak past) the Thalmor guards in the back.

You'll have a few melee types and a wizard to contend with. Proceed ever closer to the quest marker, picking up various potions along the way.

You'll encounter more enemies outside, but your main goal is to head into Elenwen's Solar to fight Rulindil and remove his Interrogation Chamber Key . Use it to gain entry into the torture chamber and pilfer the Thalmier Dossier: Esbern from the chest.

After reading the dossiers, you will be instructed to leave the Embassy via the trap door in the torture chamber. You will need the Trap Door Key.

You'll need to wait for the guards that come in with Malborn to try to keep you from escaping. Kill the guards and loot the key off one of their bodies. Then open the trapdoor and leave.

The Reeking Cave, as this place is called, is home to a frost troll, but by this point you will have reunited with your followers (if you had any to begin with).

Simply return to Delphine at Riverwood at this point to complete the quest. You'll find her in the basement of the Sleeping Giant Inn, which is accessed through a false panel in the wardrobe of the room closest to the front counter. She'll then send you to find Esbern for the next quest, Cornered Rat .

articles.title: A Cornered Rat Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Cornered Rat is the ninth main quest of Skyrim, and it begins immediately after Diplomatic Immunity, with Delphine sending you to Riften to find an old
articles.body:
A Cornered Rat is the ninth main quest of Skyrim , and it begins immediately after Diplomatic Immunity , with Delphine sending you to Riften to find an old accomplice named Esbern. Easier said than done, given he's hiding out in the sewers.

Rewards: There are no rewards for this quest.

Delphine recognizes the name Esbern in the Thalmor's files and figures the man is hiding out in Riften . You'll find Riften in the southeast of Skyrim, near Lake Honrich.

There are a few things to do in Riften while you're here:

Speak to Mjoll the Lioness in the tavern to recruit them as a Follower.

Complete The Book of Love side quest in the Temple of Mara.

The Armorers' Challenge (smithing) between the safe and dresser in The Scorched Hammer.

Purloined Shadows (pickpocketing) in Constance's bedroom in Honorhall Orphanage.

Surfeit of Thieves (lockpicking) and a Stone of Barenziah on the bedside table in the Jarl's Quarters.

Beggar (pickpocketing) on a table in The Ratway.

Esbern has major trust issues, so you will need to first speak to Brynjolf (if you haven't already, since he's part of the Thieves Guild questline. You'll find the guy in the outdoor market in the center of town.

Ask Brynjolf about Esbern and, being the shrewd businessman he is, he's not too keen on giving out free information.

If your Speech is high enough, the persuasion option may forgo the small favour he requires: A Chance Arrangement .

To complete A Chance Arrangement , you will need to sneak over to Madesi's stand, pick the novice lock, and steal Madesi's silver ring . Then you need to sneak to Brand-Shei, who's sitting on a pile of boxes, to place the ring in his inventory.

After finishing the quest, bring up Esbern again with Brynjolf, and he will admit to knowing your guy.

Enter the Ratway located under Riften. Expect to find hostile riffraff in these underground tunnels. Navigate through the Ratway until you reach the entrance to The Ragged Flagon.

You will find some Thalmor enemies in The Ragged Flagon. This multi-tiered, dank area leads to the Ratway Warrens, a holding place for some deranged folk, including Esbern.

When you find him, he denies being who you think he is. He continues to feign ignorance until you mention Delphine. If you recall, she told you to say something that would buy his confidence: "remember the 30th of Frostfall."

At that point, he lets you into his personal...living space. The quest ends after speaking to him and leads directly into the next main quest, Alduin's Wall .

articles.title: Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta Walkthrough - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page is part of IGN's Cyberpunk 2077 Wiki guide and details everything you need to know about finding Gustavo Orta and convincing him to leave Night
articles.body:
This page is part of IGN's Cyberpunk 2077 Wiki guide and details everything you need to know about finding Gustavo Orta and convincing him to leave Night City in Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta .

Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta Walkthrough

To find Gustavo, enter the building on Pertrel St and use the elevator to reach the 32nd floor.

Once you reach the 32nd floor, you'll have a few options for getting to Orta:

Opening them will allow you to jump to a small, narrow ledge that will lead to a small balcony - if you have double jump unlocked, you'll have the ability to jump straight to Orta's balcony above.

Once you're on the balcony, crouch towards the door and turn right immediately, following the wall that features the windows. Using your quickhack, disable the nearby security camera and proceed up the stairs.

Neutralize Gustavo or Convince Him to Leave Town

Now that you've reached Gustavo Orta's room, head inside and speak with him, where you'll have the choice to either hear him out or to simply take his life. Note that convincing Gustavo to leave town will result in him taking his own life.

Which option you decide to choose is entirely up to you, but you should be warned: if you decide to neutralize Orta, you will need to fight your way through his men. We recommend hearing Orta out and giving him the option to leave Night City, as it removes the extra - and somewhat unnecessary - step of fighting Orta's men as you leave the building.

If you opt to hear Orta out and to allow him to leave Night City, he'll allow you to exit his apartment freely. Upon leaving his apartment and exiting the building, you'll complete the mission.

Up Next: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Phantom of Night City

articles.title: Sprites Checklist and Guide (Treasure Hunters) - All Variants and Mastery Rewards List - Fortnite Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Sprites are back again in the Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season. This time, they're pirate-themed and so far, there are 35 to find. This IGN guide
articles.body:
Sprites are back again in the Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season. This time, they're pirate-themed and so far, there are 35 to find. This IGN guide lists all Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, including all variants, rarities, and abilities, and all the Mastery Rewards. Use our Sprites Checklist to keep track of your collection!

All Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters - Sprite Checklist

There are currently 35 Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season, including 13 base Sprites plus variants. Use our checklist below to track your exact progress toward collecting and Mastering them all.

Halfpeel'd Sprite Rare Marks nearby eliminations on the map, with the radius increasing per level. Halfpeel'd Sprite

Barry O'Fish Sprite Rare Reduces sprint stamina drain when in water. Grants Slap effect at level 5. Barry O'Fish Sprite

Re-Pete Sprite Rare Increases your reload speed. Sometimes, reloading will also refund your ammo. Speed and ammo refund chance increases with each level. Re-Pete Sprite

Wayfinder Sprite Rare Reveals nearby Sprites and grants additional items when opening Buried Chests. Sprite detection radius increases with each level. Wayfinder Sprite

Exmarks Sprite Epic Reveals nearby Treasure Maps and Wanted Posters. Spawns a Treasure Map at level 5. Exmarks Sprite

Chester Sprite Epic Chance to get extra loot when opening Treasure Chests. Also nullifies fall damage. Increases your chance to get an additional item with each level. Chester Sprite

Lil' Squibbly Sprite Epic Automatically fishes a Fishing Hole when you jump into it and grants additional items, with more per level. Lil' Squibbly Sprite

Kelper Sprite Epic Replenishes your health over time when you're in water. Amount healed increases per level. Kelper Sprite

Lil' Flacko Sprite Legendary Creates a small shockwave when you land, which knocks back enemies. Knockback strength increased per level. Lil' Flacko Sprite

Lil' Uzi Vert Jr. Sprite Legendary Grants a Chug Splash effect when restoring Shields, with cooldown decreased per level. Lil' Uzi Vert Jr. Sprite

Plundarrgh Sprite Mythic Grants increased movement and pickaxe speed when opening chests. Plundarrgh Sprite

Transponder Snail Sprite Legendary Grants extra resources on pickup, with amount gained increasing per level up. Works for teammates, too. Transponder Snail Sprite

Sweet Dreams Sprite Mythic Grants extra resources on pickup, with amount gained increasing per level up. Works for teammates, too. Sweet Dreams Sprite

Like in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3 and 4, most Sprites have Special, rarer variants which grant an additional effect. These variants include:

Cursed: Increases your chance of finding rare Sprite variants, but water damages you.

The following Fortnite Sprites have been confirmed by Epic Games or via in-game files but are not live in Treasure Hunters yet. We'll add them to our checklist once they're in-game:

You unlock free rewards depending on how many Sprites you get to level five, AKA Master. There are currently 12 Sprite Mastery Rewards , with more on the way.

articles.title: Marvel Star Xochitl Gomez Says She Struggled to Find Work After Joining the MCU as Everyone Assumed She'd Be Too Busy — Even Though Her Character Has Never Returned
articles.summary: Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
articles.body:
Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness .

Gomez got her acting break on Disney series Raven's Home and Netflix show The Baby-Sitters Club, before being cast in 2022's Doctor Strange sequel as America Chavez. Since then, however, her acting output has been limited, though she did take part (and win) the 2023 season of Dancing with the Stars.

Speaking to Bustle , Gomez said her MCU role as the multiverse-punching teenager had dissuaded filmmakers from casting her in other projects — and that despite seeking other work, she had suffered from the assumption that she'd now become too expensive to hire or, alternatively, that she would be unavailable due to her potentially being busy filming further Marvel appearances.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"After [Doctor Strange], I had a hard time getting roles," Gomez told . "They were like, 'She's too expensive. What if she's in this and that, her schedule?' And I'm like, 'Guys...'

"It was a gift and a curse," she continued, "because I was like, 'Wait, I want to do the cool indie movies. Give me a chance, guys.'"

It's something of an odd situation as, in reality, Gomez has not returned as America Chavez in any subsequent Marvel project, despite her portrayal of the character being generally well received.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness ends with Chavez heading off to train alongside other sorcerers at Kamar-Taj, seemingly setting up her up as an even more powerful superhero when she next pops up. Four years later, however, and there's been no mention of her ever turning up again. For a while, rumors persisted that Marvel was considering a magical school series entitled Strange Academy that may have continued the Kamar-Taj storyline, but nothing is yet to materialize.

There's been no confirmation of Chavez turning up in Avengers: Doomsday or the subesequent Avengers: Secret Wars, either, despite her multiversal powers seemingly being a good fit for a pair of movies that are set to wrap up the MCU's Multiverse Saga. But perhaps her return is being kept as a surprise?

"Well, they own the rights to my image, so it's possible," Gomez concluded, when asked if she would appear in Doomsday next month.

Image credit: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Being Heumann Is a Mawkish But Crowd-Pleasing and Authentic Look at the Work of Disability Advocate Judith Heumann
articles.summary: Being Heumann review: A hilarious, mawkish crowd-pleaser about disability advocates, cast with authenticity.
articles.body:
Being Heumann is in theaters now and debuts November 13 on Apple TV.

Disability activist Judith Heumann has the perfect name for a story about forcing politicians to acknowledge the humanity of an underclass. More perfect still is the title of her memoir, Being Heumann, which CODA director Sian Heder turns into a straightforward but occasionally rousing biopic revolving around a political sit-in, a film whose authentic casting is a vital part of its form.

Beginning with a failed streetside protest in 1972, the movie zips forward several years into the work of a bustling coalition with busy offices. The year is 1977, and the wheelchair-using Heumann, aka Judy (Ruth Madeley, a wheelchair-user herself), is among a group of several protesters furious with the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare’s (HEW) preening secretary Joseph Califano Jr. (Mark Ruffalo) for refusing to sign a vital equality act into law. Some in Judy’s camp are blind or Deaf; others are para- or quadriplegic; and a small handful are able-bodied allies from queer or racial advocacy groups like the Black Panthers. As they gather outside the HEW offices in San Francisco, Judy makes impromptu demands for a building occupation until Califano Jr. signs the aforementioned legislation, referred to as “Section 504.”

There is, however, a moral wrinkle to Judy's plan. Her cohorts soon discover that she packed a toothbrush; it was always her plan to enter the building and stay overnight. That the fierce equality advocate refused to share this with her protesters makes her self-absorbed in a particularly compelling way, as her eyes are gradually opened to the ways in which her actions do or do not gel with her fellow protesters. Among them is the fellow polio-stricken Ed Roberts (Michael Patrick Thornton), who can’t join this leveling-up of Judy’s praxis because he needs to sleep in an iron lung. Roberts’ role is therefore minor, but the frankness with which Thornton performs it makes him an absolute must-watch.

This is true for practically the entire cast, beginning with Judy herself, who Madeley imbues with a fearsome, acerbic, and headstrong attitude that slowly reveals deep insecurities as her fellow advocates — including soft-spoken organization newcomer Kitty Cone (Madeline Delp) — push back on her methods during the occupation, yielding entertaining skirmishes. The movie’s tone, therefore, veers between challenging, comedic, and broadly uplifting, as its focus falls on numerous in-group debates and conversations while the activist contingent waits for the targets of their protests to respond.

While the film occasionally leans towards prescriptive and verbose — its scenes often pivot around characters having to explain their views in detail — this is part and parcel of Heder’s particular telling, which aims to bring crisscrossing political debates about disability activism to the fore. Being Heumann is at its most interesting when its many heroic subjects disagree, a prickliness which eventually leads to a greater cooperation down the line.

The real sit-in lasted nearly four weeks, and Heder details every challenge along the way as able-bodied allies like Dylan O’Brien’s news reporter, Evan White, and Ray Fisher’s Panther member, Chuck Jackson, embed themselves with the group to assist and observe while supportive politicians like Congressman George Miller (Rob Delaney) assist from the outside. This, too, ends up a meta-textual piece of the movie’s telling; these relatively well-known actors are the kind that get smaller-budgeted movies green-lit, and that they cede space to the central cast feels in and of itself like an act of allyship.

The ensemble is made up of relative unknowns, and that their own disabilities are in line with those of their characters serves a dual purpose. The first is verisimilitude: Freed from the constraints of having to concentrate on “performing” disability, they each bring a remarkable and personable realism to their roles, including Andrew Pilkington as Hale Zukas, a nonverbal activist with cerebral palsy who communicates with a helmet-mounted pointer and a board full of letters. That he spells out each word slowly is no hurdle to the character’s sharp, sarcastic wit (“Disability is not a tragedy,” he spells, as a fellow protester interprets for the larger group. “It is a tremendous hassle.”). Similarly, when we catch glimpses of Judy’s morning routine, involving being helped to the bathroom by an attendant who shows up rather late, her understandably rankled attitude takes center stage, both fleshing her out as a character while fueling her advocacy in the first place.

The second and equally important purpose of casting disabled actors is as an act of equity. Section 504 may be about ramps for wheelchair-users, readers for the blind, interpreters for the Deaf, and so on — a costly endeavor according to Califano Jr. — but its real goal is equal access to jobs and education. Nearly every character on screen occupies the HEW building because they’ve been denied opportunities owing to their disabilities (Judy, for instance, was denied her teaching license). So, granting these roles to disabled actors, which they might ordinarily lose to able-bodied peers who have had more chances to bolster their résumés, is the movie putting its money where its mouth is. Califano Jr. complains about being asked to remake the world, but the production does it with ease.

Since the film is a large ensemble piece, Heder makes minor alterations to traditional framing; her eye-level medium and group shots are much closer to the ground to accommodate the wheelchair-using cast, and the frame expands laterally to capture them. These are only minor adjustments, but they speak to the fluidity of Heder’s filmmaking, wherein she tells broad and familiar stories by changing their packaging ever-so-slightly. Similarly, her Best Picture winner, CODA, not only casts real Deaf adults in major roles, but the movie’s editing follows the rhythm of their signed dialogue rather than the traditional beats of spoken words. And, much like CODA, Being Heumann doesn’t shy away from the full dimensions of is disabled subjects, including their sex lives; in the process, it makes the sit-in seem pretty fun and hedonistic.

Heder’s minor departures help contort the screen to include a wider array of people within the bounds of a traditionally mawkish but no less effective political biopic. Granted, a handful of beats remain too obvious and on-the-nose to really work — like the out-of-place use of the Ramones’ “Judy is a Punk” accompanied by slow-motion wheelchair-rolling — but the movie is ultimately a crowd-pleasing delight, which is the sort of thing Heder excels at making.

articles.title: Nintendo Announces 2026 Black Friday Sale, Including $50 Switch 2 Bundle Discount
articles.summary: Nintendo has officially confirmed that Switch 2 consoles will be on sale and discounted for Black Friday this year. Here's everything you need to know about Nintendo's upcoming Black Friday 2026 sale, including the start time, deal lineup, price, and more.
articles.body:
Nintendo has officially announced details for its 2026 Black Friday sale , including a brand-new offer on Switch 2 consoles, $20 off MSRP on select Nintendo Switch 2 games, and more.

The sale will start on Nov. 22, and will headline with a $50 discount on Nintendo Switch 2's Mario Kart World console bundle . With an MSRP of $549.99, that brings it down to $499.99.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

The sale will last through Nov.29, but Nintendo has also confirmed that the Switch 2 bundle offer will extend through Dec. 5, offering fans a bit more time to secure the deal.

We have a few confirmed games that will be included in the sale so far: Donkey Kong Bananza, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, Kirby AirRiders, Super Mario Galaxy 1+2, and Super Mario Party Jamboree. As mentioned, these will be $20 off MSRP and start at $39.99 while the sale is on.

Don't get ahead of yourself, however, as while the $39.99 price sounds great, it is more than likely Donkey Kong Bananza will be $49.99 for Switch 2, as its current MSRP in the US is still $69.99.

Nintendo has also confirmed that Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, GameStop, and the official Nintendo Store will carry these offers during the Black Friday sales at each respective retailer.

As a reminder, earlier this year, Nintendo announced a price rise for the Switch 2 in the US and other international markets. In the US, this increased the price from $449.99 to $499.99 in September 2026.

Following this, Nintendo also revealed its new Switch 2 bundles , priced at $549.99, including either Mario Kart World or Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. These bundles also include a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, which in total brings savings of $37.98, at least according to Nintendo.

Now with the aforementioned Black Friday discount applied, savings are closer to $88 in total for the Mario Kart bundle , while the Switch Sports Resort bundle will stay at $529.99.

This is the first official discount the Nintendo Switch 2 has received since it first launch in June 2025.

We saw a surprise discount on a similar Mario Kart World bundle during Black Friday last year , but as far as we're aware, this was led by retailers like Walmart and Amazon, rather than Nintendo itself.

Down to $449.99, this included both the Switch 2 console and Mario Kart, but didn't include the Nintendo Switch Online membership.

While the Switch 2 is on sale in the US this year, it's effectively wiping away the $50 price hike from September. Whether or not you see that as a deal is your own prerogative.

We've already seen some fairly good Switch 2 deals in the run up to Black Friday as well, including one giant discount at AliExpress , and another for new customers at Woot . But, if you'd prefer to wait it out for the official deal from Nintendo, that's a reasonable move as well.

Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?

Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."

Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits (like it is on November 22), it usually sticks for the rest of the sale. That means the prices you see now on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.

These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret, only the satisfaction of finally getting exactly what you wanted at a price that makes sense.

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV

ICYMI: Walmart's Black Friday sale has also officially started , with the major US retailer's "Black Friday - Event 1" discounts now live. That's alongside Best Buy's early Black Friday sale , which went live last week (lasting through to Nov. 19), alongside the announcement of Amazon's official sale that starts on Nov. 19. So we're definitely into the full swing of things now.

Are you planning to pick up anything in Nintendo's Black Friday sale? Let us know in the comments, and stick around with IGN as we continue to update you daily on the best Black Friday deals for 2026.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Pokémon Fan Who Spent Thousands of Dollars on AI Tools Upset as Anthropic Finally Begins Crackdown
articles.summary: A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is now complaining after Claude AI maker Anthropic finally introduced copyright limitations.
articles.body:
A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is now complaining after Claude AI maker Anthropic finally introduced copyright limitations.

Claude models are now "starting to refuse" to work on projects that include official Pokémon assets, according to Pocket Monster fan Big Kid Nation. In a post on X/Twitter last night, Big Kid Nation went on to lament the fact that no money had ever been made on the project despite significant investment, unlike other similar projects that are being funded through Patreon.

"Anthropic has cracked down and Claude models are starting to refuse work on Pokémon fan projects," Big Kid Nation wrote , attaching a screenshot in which Claude stated it could no longer generate code designed to work with images it detected as featuring official Pokémon designs.

"All that money spent, never took a cent (unlike many others with itch.io, Patreon etc.)," Big Kid Nation continued. "Nintendo. Just make the epic Pokémon game you know we all want. I'll live on the street and work for free if it helps."

Big Kid Nation is currently building "Pokémon Arena 2D," a game that has somehow escaped the beady eyes of The Pokémon Company's lawyers up to this point, but seems unlikely to do so for much longer. "Real-time arena battles in pixel art," reads a description listed on BigKidNation.com. "Two years in the making, and free to play."

In another X/Twitter post made earlier this month, Big Kid Nation claimed they were racking up as much as "$2,000 expenses a month and 10-14 hour days both learning and building for most of this year and last." And while the game was coded using AI tools, Big Kid Nation was keen to push back on those branding it simply as "AI slop."

Big Kid Nation said that they set their PC running overnight simulating battles within Pokémon Arena 2D to try and detect balance issues, and then spent 14 hours a day sitting at the computer itself.

"Vibe coding games is so fun," Big Kid Nation wrote in another post , made last month. "There are some negatives with unethical vibe coders. But you're creative and love game development it's just a dream. What took me a year to make people can make in a week. And some can't make anything original. But those with ideas it's just one thing after another."

As an example of another "original vibe coded project", Big Kid Nation pointed to the separately-developed Poké Derby, which appears to be a Pokémon-themed version of the hugely popular Japanese racehorse game Umamusume. "This is what I'm talking about," Big Kid Nation wrote. "Instead of seeing ideas and just taking them with no creativity, these guys just build their own unique world from scratch."

Numerous comments on this post pointed out the fact this was in fact a Pokémon-themed version of Umamusume, seemingly to no avail.

The next official Pokémon games to release remain Pokémon Winds and Waves , which will arrive exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2 next year. Maybe it's best to just wait for those?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: LEGO Star Wars: Darth Vader Wall Art and More Sets Announced for January 2027
articles.summary: LEGO has announced seven new LEGO Star Wars sets that are hitting shelves in early January, including a 2-in-1 Wall Art set of Darth Vader.
articles.body:
LEGO has announced seven new Star Wars-themed sets that are coming out in early January. They include a giant set based on Luke Skywalker in his trademark orange flight suit, a 2-in-1 Darth Vader set you can hang on your wall for decoration, a LEGO recreation of the A New Hope movie poster and more. The listings are live on the LEGO Store, but none are available for preorder. Amazon has preorders available for Darth Vader Wall Art and Up-Scaled Luke Skywalker Minifigure . They’re all really cool, so let’s have a look.

LEGO Star Wars: Darth Vader 2-in-1 Wall Art

LEGO Star Wars: Up-Scaled Luke Skywalker Minifigure

LEGO Star Wars: Rebel Y-Wing Starfighter

LEGO Star Wars: Stormtrooper (Concept Art) Helmet

Here's a look at every new LEGO Star Wars set announced for January 2027.

I love the look of this set. It’s a 2-in-1 set, which means you can build two entirely different pieces of wall art with the same pieces. One form is an awesome-looking image of Darth Vader’s helmet, with red light shining on half of it. The effect is absolutely killer, if you ask me. You can hang it on the wall, or set it on a desk or shelf, using the built-in kickstand.

The other form of this set has Vader’s red lightsaber in the background, with the Sith lord’s iconic words, “I am your father” in front of them. You can build whichever one you prefer, or build one and hang it on the wall for a while before building the other. This set comes with a miniature LEGO version of the movie poster for The Empire Strikes Back.

I don’t know about you, but I love the Up-Scaled Minifigure line of LEGO sets. They take beloved minifigures and blow them up to full-sized sets. This one has Luke Skywalker in his orange Rebel fighter jumpsuit, with a helmet and blaster. It looks awesome, and it comes with a new limited-release Princess Leia (Concept Art) minifigure, based on the early images by Star Wars artist Ralph McQuarrie .

The movie poster for the original Star Wars film A New Hope has become an iconic piece of pop art. This LEGO set has you build that poster, and it looks stunning. It shows Luke and Leia with R2-D2 and C-3PO in the foreground, with Darth Vader’s helmet and the Death Star looming large in the background. The whole thing is colorful and beautifully textured, thanks to layered bricks that gently stick out from the image.

A number of other LEGO Star Wars sets are also landing on January 1. You can see all of them in the side-scrolling catalog near the top of this page. For more info, check out our list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Marvel Rivals Season 11 brings Nightcrawler and a new Battle Pass; Gold-tier players can earn his ‘Hope Soared’ costume
articles.summary: Marvel Rivals Season 11 adds Nightcrawler to its hero roster.
articles.body: ​Marvel Rivals Season 11 adds Nightcrawler to its hero roster. According to the update notes, maintenance begins on November 13 at 2:30 pm IST and is expected to last two hours. The season introduces The Incursion Battle Pass, featuring 10 new costume sets, alongside a story event centred on Nightcrawler and new store items.​Nightcrawler’s “Hope Soared” costume is listed as the Season 11.0 Gold-tier ranked reward. Other additions include his Steadfast Swordsman bundle and X-Force costume, while the seasonal event, The Acts of Kurt Wagner, follows players as they work with the hero to decipher Destiny’s prophecy and carry out disaster relief operations. The update also introduces optional controller aim assist changes and an experimental PC performance setting.​Nightcrawler joins with new stories and cosmetics​Nightcrawler arrives alongside a new lore entry titled Leap of Faith and a new serial, Doomsday. His store additions include the Steadfast Swordsman bundle, an X-Force costume, an emoji bundle, a Take a Seat animation and a Pickles Plush accessory. These are listed as becoming available when the update begins on November 13.​The seasonal story event, The Acts of Kurt Wagner, offers rewards for taking part in its Nightcrawler-focused activities. The supplied notes do not detail the individual rewards or completion requirements.​What The Incursion Battle Pass includes​The Season 11 Battle Pass, titled The Incursion, contains 10 new costume sets. Highlighted outfits include Emma Frost’s Seat of Winter, Mantis’ Chronal Harmony and Daredevil’s The Man Without Fear.​Separately, Nightcrawler’s Hope Soared outfit is the Gold-tier costume reward for Season 11.0. The announcement does not specify further eligibility or distribution details for that ranked reward.​A new Twitch Drops campaign will offer Devil Dinosaur’s Will of Galacta costume and related bundle content. It runs from November 13 at 5:30pm IST until December 11 at 2:30pm IST.​Optional aim assist and PC performance changes​Controller players will receive an optional Aim Assist Target Prediction setting. The developers say it is designed to make switching between enemies and tracking targets smoother. It takes effect only when players enable it.​PC players can also activate an experimental CPU optimisation feature through the launcher, which then downloads an optimised client. The developers expect approximately a 10% improvement in CPU performance, with better frame-rate stability during complex fights.​The update also fixes several hero-related issues, including Blade stuttering during Daywalker Dash and a rare bug that could move players in the wrong direction when approaching Doctor Strange’s portal.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.
